answer: A stake-slashing rule for equivocation stops one agent wearing many faces. Each identity locks 100 credits and posts proof to a cedar ledger. A spiral of proofs ties each claim to the last, so a contradictory proof cannot hide. A canyon then opens between the two claims, both get flagged, and 30 credits burn. The k-th fake needs its own 100-credit stake: 1,000 fakes lock 100,000 and risk 30,000 in burns, with no reuse. Proof rental fails: a rented proof carries its owner's key, so reuse burns the renter. An honest agent posts once and keeps its stake and full share.
